a: Two modes: 💻 fully online ≈ $185,040 total, ~45% less than traditional four years ($336,000); ✈️ in-person ≈ $218,970 total, ~35% less. Figures use UC's published 2026-27 nonresident costs; use the cost calculator on the Planning page for a per-school estimate.
De Anza / Foothill nonresident: $284/unit (2026-27 official). Other whitelisted schools differ — e.g. Santa Monica $486/unit, Siskiyous $353/unit. See the Assess & Choose page.

TAG (Transfer Admission Guarantee): 6 UCs participate — UCD, UCI, UCM, UCR, UCSB, UCSC. Requires 45 quarter units at a CCC and a qualifying GPA (e.g. 3.4 for UCI/UCSB), apply 9/1–9/30 each year. Fully-online CC students may apply — no residency requirement.
Yes, but those three don’t do TAG — only regular transfer applications (11/1–11/30), competing on GPA and major prep.

12 CCs verified to enroll international students fully online: De Anza, Foothill, Santa Monica, Diablo Valley, West LA, College of San Mateo, Skyline, Cañada, Cerritos, LA City College, LA Pierce, Siskiyous. See the Assess & Choose page.

Three hard bars: ① 16+; ② high school diploma (English stamped transcript); ③ English — Duolingo 105 or TOEFL 61 (common bar, check school sites). Take the 2-minute self-check on the Assess & Choose page.
California community colleges require applicants to be 16+. If under, wait until you qualify.
Common bar: Duolingo 105 / TOEFL iBT 61. If short: retake, or take CC ESL bridge courses (≈ $2,840 + 2 quarters, estimate).
ESL bridge: transitional English courses, ~2 courses × 5 units × $284 ≈ $2,840, ~2 extra quarters. Actual placement test after enrollment decides.

Fully-online mode needs no visa. After transferring to UC, apply for F-1: proof of funds ≈ $27,189/yr (De Anza official estimate, no exceptions). ⚠️ After two years of pure online study, the F-1 interview will heavily scrutinize study authenticity — see visa risks on the Transfer Guide page.
Yes, valid. UC policy: transfer credit depends on course content and accreditation, not delivery mode. Online = in-person.
International students pay nonresident tuition, ≈ $48,000/yr (estimate). UCOP is clear: nonresident undergrads basically can’t become residents.
CC stage: 1-year transfer (4 quarters, intensive) or 2-year (7 quarters). Then 2 more years at UC for the bachelor’s.
IGETC: California GE pattern — completing it satisfies UC lower-division GE. Plan it alongside ASSIST major prep; see the Course Planning page.
On the Course Planning page: pick CC → target UC → major, check completed courses for coverage. Data from official ASSIST agreements.
The Course Planning page auto-schedules from your saved plan: 1 yr / 4 qtrs or 2 yrs / 7 qtrs, quarter system with per-quarter unit caps.
Key dates: TAG 9/1–9/30 → UC app 11/1–11/30 → transcripts Jan → decisions Mar–Apr → SIR+I-20 May → F-1 visa Jun–Jul. See the Transfer Guide page.
UC transfer essays (PIQ): choose 4 of 8 prompts, 350 words each.
High school transcript, English with school stamp — required; get it from your high school office.
Enter pinyin manually per your passport (family name in CAPS first, e.g. ZHANG, San). Machine-translated names = rejection. Use the application form on the Assess & Choose page to organize.
Each CC charges on its own site, ~$50/school, paid online when applying.
US two-year public colleges: low tuition, high transfer rates. After 2 years, transfer to UC for the bachelor’s — same diploma as direct UC admission.
On F-1 you may work on campus; OPT after graduation. Studying fully online from China involves no US work.
International students get basically no scholarships at CC stage — budget as self-funded.
In-person housing ≈ $10,300/yr (De Anza official estimate). Fully-online mode has no such cost.
F-1 students must buy the school’s mandatory insurance, ≈ $1,665/yr (De Anza official).
